title: Managed Identity with Azure SQL
description: Authenticate to Azure SQL Database using managed identities instead of SQL authentication passwords.

data.text: Azure SQL supports SQL authentication (username and password) and Entra ID authentication. Entra ID authentication includes managed identities, which remove the need to store SQL credentials anywhere.
When using a managed identity, Azure SQL validates the token issued by Entra ID. You create a contained database user mapped to the external identity.

data.title: Azure SQL Auth Methods
items: SQL Authentication — username/password stored in SQL
Entra ID Universal with MFA — interactive user login
Managed Identity — passwordless for Azure-hosted apps

data.title: Create a Contained User for a Managed Identity
data.content: Map a managed identity to a database user so it can connect to Azure SQL.

data.title: Connection String with Managed Identity (C#)
data.content: Use SqlClient with Azure.Identity for passwordless SQL authentication.

data.title: Connect an App to Azure SQL
data.description: Enable managed identity on an App Service, create an Azure SQL database user, and query data without a SQL password.
steps: Create an Azure SQL database and set an Azure AD admin.
Enable managed identity on your App Service.
Run T-SQL to create a contained user FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER.
Update your app to use DefaultAzureCredential with SqlClient.
data.expectedOutcome: Your app connects to Azure SQL using a managed identity with no password stored anywhere.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Managed identity removes the need for SQL authentication passwords.
CREATE USER ... FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER maps an Entra ID identity to SQL.
DefaultAzureCredential + SqlClient provides a clean passwordless pattern.
